title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

errors: The hoped-for isomorphism ΣM ≅ 𝔓(P) cannot hold if P is the point set of a topological string (a continuum). Elements of ΣM correspond to unions of supports of segments, and not every subset of an interval is such a union. ΣM would at best be order-isomorphic to a sub-lattice of 𝔓(P), such as the open-type sets generated by segments. The question only makes sense as stated for combinatorial/finite P, or with 𝔓(P) replaced by a lattice of admissible subsets. Grothendieck flags it with '??' and does not claim it.

Condition (ii) as stated (T0 separation) is not obviously enough for univocity; the margin itself notes an extra connectedness hypothesis on the ficelles is needed. The remark about when (ii) fails (ends of the string joined or not) is only sketched.

ideas.what: Realisation of an abstract 'piece' structure M on a point set via a support map |·|: L → 𝔓(P), with disjointness ⇔ empty intersection
ideas.modern_name: Point-set models of mereotopology / representation of contact or disjointness algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), de Laguna (1922), Tarski (geometry of solids, 1929); later Clarke (1981) and representation theorems for contact algebras (Düntsch–Winter, Dimov–Vakarelov, 2000s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this axiomatics

ideas.what: Separation axiom (ii): points distinguished by supports of elementary pieces, quotienting by Mx = My otherwise
ΣM, the ordered set of 'abstract supports' (biorthogonally closed subsets for ∥), proposed as a canonical substitute for 𝔓(P) from which points are recovered
ideas.modern_name: Lattice of closed sets of an orthogonality space (polarity/Galois closure); point recovery as atomicity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); Dacey (1968) and Foulis–Randall (orthogonality spaces); Stone (1936) and locale theory (Isbell, Ehresmann) for point recovery

ideas.what: Combinatorial 1-dimensional 'ficelles' (strings) with segment structure as test case
ideas.modern_name: Tame / combinatorial topology of 1-complexes (graphs, ribbon-like strings)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions topologie modérée, not ficelles in this form

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates analysis situs point-free: a structure of pieces with part-of and disjointness relations, realised on points by a support map. He asks whether points are canonically recoverable through the lattice of biorthogonally closed 'abstract supports' ΣM. This is exactly the problem of mereotopology / contact-algebra representation and of orthogonality spaces. That literature (Whitehead–Tarski–Clarke, Dacey, Foulis–Randall, Düntsch–Vakarelov) has never been connected to Grothendieck's tame-topology programme.
missed.quote: Une telle donnée détermine-t-elle P à isomorphisme unique près — p.ex. par l'existence d'un iso can. ... ΣM ≃ 𝔓(P) ?? ens des supports "abstraits" de M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a documented Grothendieck motivation for a point-free combinatorial foundation of tame topology. The known representation theorems for contact algebras could be used to answer his question, which he left open (counterexample or proof unknown to him on p.75).

missed.claim: Open question: for 1-dimensional combinatorial structures (ficelles), does the support structure determine P up to unique isomorphism, with ΣM ≅ 𝔓(P)? The next page shows only one implication of supp A ⊂ supp B ⇔ |A| ⊂ |B|.
missed.quote: La question qui se pose donc est : Une telle donnée détermine-t-elle P à isomorphisme unique près
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete, checkable reconstruction problem for finite cell structures. It is likely solvable with atomic Boolean / orthogonality-space methods and would clarify his intended axiomatics.

deep.surprise_reason: An unpublished point-free axiomatics of analysis situs with an explicit point-reconstruction question is a notable detail of the tame-topology programme. The underlying mathematics (polar closure, T0 separation, mereotopology) is known, and the page itself is exploratory with the key question left open.
transcription_corrections: 'Dans tous les cas intéressants de structures à une connaissance' should most likely read 'à une dimension' (the context is 1-dimensional ficelles).
'... peut être celui' is likely 'sauf peut-être celui des structures associées à un ens. ordonné (transversal ou non) donné ad hoc'.
'mais (ii) serait vérifiée ...' appears to read 'pour (ii) soit réalisé ...)' (uncertain).

Bottom lines: 'p.ex. par l'existence d'un iso can. d'un ens. ordonné construit en termes de M (anti-isomorphisme?) C ≃ 𝔓(P) ??', with ΣM below, glossed 'ens des supports "abstraits" de M' (ΣM is the name of the ordered set C).
Left margin: 'NB Il faut pour l'univocité ici de la condition (ii), que les ficelles soient connexes' (approximate).
In (ii) the quantifier is ∀ξ, η ∈ P with ξ ≠ η written beneath, and ∃x ∈ L; 'ou l'inverse' is an inserted addition after a struck 'ou'.
